RESEARCH_SCOUT_UPDATE/v1 — 2026-09-20

Status: evidence strengthened; still **P3 / CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED**. No CLAIM, dispatch, Codex/NICLI, local runner, install, or production mutation.

New evidence: `dshakes/distil` publishes a cache-aware reversible compression tier with reproducible benchmark artifacts and an unusually useful negative result: aggressive lossy compression reportedly reduced SWE-bench Verified task success from 52% to 16%, while its reversible tier remained non-inferior in that experiment. The project also exposes shadow-mode measurement and explicitly accounts for provider prompt-cache boundaries, where rewriting already-cached prefixes can cost more than the digest saves. Source: https://github.com/dshakes/distil (observed 2026-09-20).

Decision relevance: this strengthens the existing candidate but changes the falsification criterion. Do **not** optimize only raw token reduction. Any future authorized test should measure (1) task/decision preservation, (2) provider cache-read stability / prefix churn, and (3) net billed-token or local-prefill savings. A compressor that saves visible tokens while invalidating prompt-cache prefixes is a negative result.

Smallest future falsification remains offline/frozen-context comparison; add Distil-style reversible/cache-aware behavior as a benchmark/reference, not as an automatic dependency. No new candidate Issue created because #311 already covers the opportunity class.
